questions.question: Describe how three test tubes can be set up to show that both oxygen and water are needed for rusting, and state the expected results.
questions.expected_answer: A: nail in tap water open to air (water and oxygen) rusts. B: nail in boiled water with a layer of oil (water, no oxygen) does not rust. C: nail in dry air with calcium chloride and a stopper (oxygen, no water) does not rust. So both are needed.

questions.question: Explain why galvanised steel still does not rust when scratched, but painted steel does.
questions.expected_answer: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so at a scratch the zinc corrodes in preference to the iron (sacrificial protection). Paint is only a barrier; once scratched, water and oxygen reach the iron and it rusts.

questions.question: Give a suitable rust-prevention method for a bicycle chain and for a tap, with a reason for each.
questions.expected_answer: Bicycle chain: oil or grease, because it moves and paint would rub off. Tap: chromium electroplating, because it gives a shiny, attractive, water-resistant surface.
